Despite everything I'm about to say I still start my games at level 1 because it's what my players apparently want. What they want takes precedent over something that doesn't really affect me.

What level should you start the game at depends on the game. If you want rags to riches commoner to hero type story you can start them at level ZERO where they only have an allowance to buy equipment and background/race features.

If you want to continue a story that you left behind, or pick up somewhere huge then starting at level 11 is an option where every class is at borderline peak power.

Level 1 is a poor choice for many reasons;

  • Over-simplified.

Combat is a chore and nobody really has any options. This is great for brand new players but mind-numbingly boring for experienced ones.

  • Lore handwaving

Beginning at level 1 means your Bard hasn't graduated college. It means the Wizard hasn't finished his school. The Paladin has no oath. The Rogue has no specialty/profession. The Warlock has no pact.

This is great if you plan to actually RP out these specific events occuring, but usually it's handwaved and nobody actually does that.

It's also a bit of a hassle to RP out 5 distinct character defining moments in the space of around 5-10 sessions it make take to level from 1 to 3. There would be almost no room for the game itself, just character moments/sessions/plots.

  • Lethality

Level 1 is terribly balanced where people instantly die to crits all the time. It's not fun to pour your heart into a character and have them ripped away due to an unlucky roll in sessions 1-4.

The death isn't even meaningful at that point, it's just a hassle to have to babysit the players and fudge rolls to ensure a wayward crit doesn't actually kill them but just downs them instead. For example anyone with a longbow can do a critical d8, which could be 16 damage. 16 damage instantly kills a lot of characters at full health, let alone in the middle of a combat.

  • It's so fast you may as well skip it

If you go by the book and XP, levels 1-3 pass in a couple of sessions. You may as well just skip the tutorial and get into it right away.

For example, Death House in Curse of Strahd took my group 2 or 3 sessions and it gets you from 1 to 3. If you level up every single session it takes all the meaning away from it and actually gets people in a bad state of mind where they're expecting level ups more often than they should at later levels.

  • Multiclassing

Multiclass builds literally cannot exist at level 1. This leads to characters such as an Assassin Rogue/Death Cleric mixture having nothing from one side of their class for a while, making playing the character a bit weird if your backstory/personality is heavily driven by your multiclass.

Another great example is a Bard/Paladin multiclass either not having Inspiration/spells OR not having Lay on Hands/Divine Sense/armour at level 1.

  • Samey

Everyone is basically the same at level 1. People are literally identical if they both share the same class.

If your group is supposed to be say, a 5 Rogue hit squad party and you start them at level 1 then that's a huge mistake.

Start them at 3 and you can feel the differences between an Assassin, a Thief, an Arcane Trickster and a Scout very tangibly and everyone has their own identity, roles, skills and specialities.
